record.title: Grinshpun–Sárközy conjecture on tiling bounded-degree graph sequences
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}={F_1,F_2,\dots\}$ be a graph sequence with $v(F_i)=i$ and maximum degree $\Delta(F_i)\leq\Delta$ for all $i$. For an $r$-edge coloured complete graph, let $\tau_r(\mathcal{F})$ be the least $s$ such that its vertex set has a monochromatic $\mathcal{F}$-tiling of size at most $s$, where a monochromatic $\mathcal{F}$-tiling consists of monochromatic subgraphs, each isomorphic to an element of $\mathcal{F}$, whose vertex sets partition the complete graph's vertex set.

**Grinshpun–Sárközy conjecture.** For every positive integer $r$ there exists a constant $C_r$ such that, for every $\Delta\geq 2$ and every $\Delta$-bounded graph sequence $\mathcal{F}$,

$$
tau_r(\mathcal{F})\leq \exp(\Delta^{C_r}).
$$

The conjecture concerns the finiteness and quantitative growth of the tiling number for more than two colours. Corsten and Mendonça later proved finiteness with a triple-exponential bound, and the paper proves the stronger bound $\tau_r(\mathcal{F})\leq\exp(C_r\Delta)$ for bipartite bounded-degree graph sequences, but the full conjecture for general sequences is not resolved here.

record.title: The NFM separated-eigenvector conjecture under Dirichlet noise
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,W)$ be generated using the node-feature model (NFM), with simplex distribution given by a Dirichlet distribution with constant parameter $\bm{\alpha}$. For $j\in[k]$, define

$$
V_j':= \{i\in[n]:\theta^i_j\geq t(k,\bm{\alpha})\},\qquad
\Theta_j:=\Theta(V_j',:).
$$

**NFM separated-eigenvector conjecture.** There exists a scalar $t(k,\bm{\alpha})\in(0.5,1/\sqrt{2})$ such that, for every $j\in[k]$, with probability not converging to $0$ as $n\to\infty$, the largest eigenvalue of

$$
4.4\Theta_j\Theta_j^T-2.2E
$$

is well separated from the remaining eigenvalues and its corresponding eigenvector is positive.

The conjecture formalizes the computational observation that strong-node subgraphs have a dominant positive spectral direction, which could support robust identification of cluster structure under asymmetric noise.

record.title: The off-diagonal book Ramsey random-bound conjecture for two books
record.statement:
Let $B_m^{(2)}$ denote the book graph consisting of $m$ triangles sharing a common edge, and let $r(B_{cn}^{(2)},B_n^{(2)})$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that every red-blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph $K_N$ contains a red copy of $B_{cn}^{(2)}$ or a blue copy of $B_n^{(2)}$. The random bound is $(\sqrt{c}+1)^2n+o(n)$. **Random-bound conjecture.** For every $c<1$, there exists some $\beta=\beta(c)>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, 
$$
r(B_{cn}^{(2)},B_n^{(2)})\geq\bigl((\sqrt{c}+1)^2+\beta\bigr)n.
$$
 Thus, for every fixed $c<1$, the random bound is not tight. This is part of the open problem of understanding $r(B_{cn}^{(2)},B_n^{(2)})$ for $c\in(1/6,1)$ as $n\to\infty$; the paper notes that its methods do not determine the threshold $c_1(2)$ and suggests that the random bound may never be tight for $c<1$.
record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox and Yuval Wigderson, “Off-diagonal book Ramsey numbers”, arXiv:2110.14483 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.14483

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2021). “Of course, this conjecture is really only the tip of an iceberg, with the general open question being to understand $r(B_{cn}\up 2,B_n \up 2)$ for $c\in (1/6,1)$ and $n\to \infty$.”

record.title: Sparse average-case k-SUM conjecture
record.statement:
In the $(k,N,r)$-SUM problem, the input consists of $r$ elements $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, independently and uniformly chosen from $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$. The goal is to find an ordered $k$-tuple of distinct indices $K=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\}$ such that

$$
\sum_{j\in K}z_j=0,
$$

where the sum is over $\mathbb{Z}$. The sparse regime has only a few solutions on average, with $r^k\approx N$. **Sparse average-case $k$-SUM conjecture.** Any algorithm that solves the $(k,N,r)$-SUM problem with $r=N^{1/k}$ and probability $\Omega_k(1)$ has expected running time at least

$$
T=\Omega_k\left(r^{\lceil k/2\rceil-o(1)}\right).
$$

The conjecture is presented as folklore hardness of the uniform distribution under a standard computational model and underlies the paper's conditional optimality results for dense $k$-SUM.

record.title: Kawasaki dynamics mixing conjecture for the fixed-magnetization Ising model
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$, and consider the fixed-magnetization Ising model with inverse temperature $\beta$ and magnetization parameter $\eta$. The Kawasaki dynamics has two versions: local flip dynamics, proposing swaps of spins across an edge, and global flip dynamics, proposing swaps of arbitrary spins. Let $\beta_c(\Delta)$ and $\eta_c(\Delta,\beta)$ denote the threshold parameters in the paper.

**Kawasaki dynamics mixing conjecture.** For $\beta<\beta_c(\Delta)$, the Kawasaki dynamics mix in time polynomial in $n$ for any fixed magnetization and any graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta$. For $\beta>\beta_c(\Delta)$ and $|\eta|>\eta_c(\Delta,\beta)$, they mix in time polynomial in $n$ for any fixed magnetization $k\geq\eta n$ and any such graph. In both cases, the global flip dynamics mix in time $O(n\log n)$.

This conjecture concerns the efficiency of a standard local Markov-chain sampler for the fixed-magnetization Ising model, complementing the paper’s approximation results. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture remains open; the relation between the one-sentence rapid-mixing claim and the more detailed parameterized formulation should be checked.

record.title: The multicolor book graph size Ramsey number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $B_n^{(k)}$ denote the book graph consisting of $k$ triangles sharing a common edge, with the shared edge contained in $k$ pages, each having $n$ vertices in the relevant book parameter as used in the paper. For a graph $H$ and integer $q\geq 2$, let $\hat r(H;q)$ be the minimum number of edges in a graph such that every $q$-edge-coloring contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and let $r(K_k;q-1)$ be the $(q-1)$-color Ramsey number of the complete graph $K_k$. **Multicolor book graph size Ramsey conjecture.** Fix $q\geq 3$. For every $k\geq 2$ and all sufficiently large $n$, 
$$
\hat r(B_n^{(k)};q)=\Theta\left(q^k\cdot n^2\cdot r(K_k;q-1)\right).
$$
 This extends the paper's two-color book-graph results to fixed multicolor settings; the conjecture is presented as an open direction, and the required order of magnitude is not established in the source.

record.title: Uniform minimization conjecture for light-traffic coefficients
record.statement:
Consider a redundancy system with $N$ servers and edge-selection probabilities $P=(p_{\{i,j\}})_{i,j}$, where $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and $i\ne j$. For each $q\geq 0$, let $\alpha_q(P)$ denote the coefficient governing the light-traffic probability of having at least $q$ jobs. Let $P'=(p'_{\{i,j\}})_{i,j}$ be the uniform policy, with

$$
p'_{\{i,j\}}=\frac{1}{\binom{N}{2}}.
$$

**Uniform minimization conjecture.** For every $q\geq 0$, the coefficient under the uniform policy equals the minimum over all edge-selection probability vectors:

$$
\alpha_q^*\coloneqq\alpha_q(P')=\min\left\{\alpha_q(P)\mid P=(p_{\{i,j\}})_{i,j}\right\}.
$$

This optimization conjecture would imply the uniform sampling dominance conjecture in the light-traffic regime through the stated comparison of tail probabilities. The coefficients are continuous functions on the compact set of edge-selection probabilities, so a minimum exists; what remains open is proving that the uniform policy attains it for every $q$.

record.title: Local Irregularity Conjecture for the locally irregular chromatic index
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{T}^{\prime}$ be the family consisting of all odd-length paths, all odd-length cycles, and the graphs obtained from the triangle by the recursive construction described in the source: identify a degree-$2$ vertex belonging to a triangle with an end-vertex of a path, whose other end is identified with a vertex of a triangle. For a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)$ be the smallest number of colors in a locally irregular edge-coloring of $G$. **Local Irregularity Conjecture.** For every connected graph $G\notin\mathfrak{T}^{\prime}$, one has

$$
\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)\leq 3.
$$

This conjecture concerns the three-color bound for connected graphs outside the known family of non-colorable graphs. The paper exhibits a bow-tie cactus with locally irregular chromatic index $4$, showing that the broader formulation is false; the stated conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The large Galois orbits conjecture for endomorphism-generic special subvarieties
record.statement:
Let $g\geq 3$, let $C$ be an irreducible algebraic curve in $\mathcal{A}_g$, and let $S$ be the smallest special subvariety of $\mathcal{A}_g$ containing $C$. Let $\Omega$ be the set of special subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ of simple PEL type I or II and dimension at most $\dim(S)-2$, and let $\Sigma$ be the set of points in $\mathcal{A}_g(\mathbb{C})$ that are endomorphism generic in some $Z\in\Omega$. Let $L$ be a finitely generated subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ over which $C$ is defined.

**Large Galois orbits conjecture.** There exist positive constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that, for every $s\in C\cap\Sigma$,

$$
\#\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{C}/L)\cdot s\geq C_1\lvert\operatorname{disc}(\operatorname{End}(A_s))\rvert^{C_2}.
$$

This is presented as the natural generalisation of the earlier large Galois orbits conjecture and is used to deduce finiteness in a Zilber--Pink setting. Its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The bosonic and fermionic polynomial degree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ indistinguishable bosons have $G={\rm SU}(N)$ with $N={{n+k-1}\choose{k}}$, and let $k$ indistinguishable fermions have $G={\rm SU}(K)$ with $K={{n}\choose{k}}$. In both cases, let $H\cong {\rm SU}(n)$ and

$$
\mathfrak{t}\cong\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\ \middle|\ \sum_{j=1}^n x_j=0\right\}.
$$

For bosons and fermions, respectively, write

$$
\Delta_{\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{h}}(x)=P_{\mathrm{bos}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n),\qquad \Delta_{\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{h}}(x)=P_{\mathrm{fer}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n),
$$

where these are homogeneous polynomials on the restriction to $\mathfrak{t}$ of the standard coordinates. **The bosonic and fermionic polynomial degree conjecture.** In the setting of the bosonic density formula (respectively, the fermionic density formula), the minimum degree $\ell+2$ of $\Delta_{\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{h}}$ restricted to any affine line in $\mathfrak{t}$ on which it does not uniformly vanish is equal to the degree of $P_{\mathrm{bos}}$ (respectively, $P_{\mathrm{fer}}$) in any one of the individual variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. This conjecture concerns the degree governing the density formula for the quantum marginal problems of indistinguishable bosons and fermions; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: Popular-difference density conjecture for three-point matrix patterns in the integer lattice
record.statement:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be $2\times2$ matrices with integer entries such that $M_2-M_1$ has full rank. For any $\alpha,\varepsilon>0$, there exists $N_0=N_0(\alpha,\varepsilon)\in\mathbb N$ such that, whenever $N\ge N_0$ and $A\subseteq\\{1,\dots,N\\}^2$ satisfies $|A|\ge\alpha N^2$, there is a vector $\vec n\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $M_1\vec n,M_2\vec n\ne0$ for which

$$
\left|\left\\{\vec x\in\mathbb Z^2:\{\vec x,\vec x+M_1\vec n,\vec x+M_2\vec n\\}\subseteq A\right\\}\right|>(\alpha^3-\varepsilon)N^2.
$$

**Popular-difference density conjecture.** The displayed lower bound holds for every pair of matrices satisfying the stated full-rank condition. The conjecture is a finitary form of the corresponding Khintchine-type recurrence question for $\mathbb Z^2$ and would determine a broad class of popular difference densities; the general three-point matrix-pattern problem is described as open.

record.title: Maximum Wiener index conjecture for directed grids
record.statement:
Let $G_{m,n}=P_m\Box P_n$ be the Cartesian product of paths on $m,n\geq 2$ vertices. Let ${D}_{m,n}$ be the orientation of $G_{m,n}$ with all $P_m$-layers oriented up except the last $P_m$-layer, which is oriented down, and all $P_n$-layers oriented to the left except the first $P_n$-layer, which is oriented to the right. Write $W_{\rm max}(G_{m,n})$ for the maximum Wiener index over all orientations of $G_{m,n}$, and $W({D}_{m,n})$ for the Wiener index of ${D}_{m,n}$. **Maximum Wiener index conjecture.** For every $m,n\geq 2$, we have

$$
W_{\rm max}(G_{m,n})=W({D}_{m,n}).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the natural generalization of the orientation known to maximize the Wiener index of the ladder graph $L_n=P_2\Box P_n$ also maximizes the Wiener index for every directed grid. The ladder case was proved by Kraner Šumenjak et al.; the general case is presented as a conjecture.

record.title: The bounded-exception conjecture for Markoff surface orbits
record.statement:
Let $a,k\in\mathbb Z$, and let

$$
\mathcal M_{a,k}: x^2+y^2+z^2=axyz+k
$$

be the Markoff surface over $\mathbb Z$, with $\mathcal G_{\mathcal M}$ the group generated by the three involutions, double sign changes, and coordinate permutations. **Bounded-exception conjecture.** (a) There is a constant $M_1(a,k)$ such that for every prime $p\nmid a$,

$$
\#\mathcal M_{a,k}(\mathbb F_p)\leq \#\bigl(\text{largest $\mathcal G_{\mathcal M}$-orbit in $\mathcal M_{a,k}(\mathbb F_p)$}\bigr)+M_1(a,k).
$$

(b) If $\#\mathcal M_{a,k}(\mathbb Z)=\infty$, then there is a constant $M_2(a,k)$ such that for every prime $p\nmid a$,

$$
\#\mathcal M_{a,k}(\mathbb F_p)\leq \#\bigl(\mathcal M_{a,k}(\mathbb Z)\bmod p\bigr)+M_2(a,k).
$$

One may further ask whether $M_1(a,k)$ and $M_2(a,k)$ can be chosen independently of $a$ and $k$. The source presents these assertions as conjectures motivated by finite orbits and lifting questions; no resolution is given.

record.title: Presentation conjecture for Dehn quandles of Artin groups
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a generating set and let

$$
\mathcal{A}=\langle S\mid (st)_{m_{st}}=(ts)_{m_{ts}}\text{ for }s,t\in S\text{ with }s\neq t\rangle
$$

be an Artin group. For quandle elements, write $(s*t)_m$ for the alternating product of $s$ and $t$ under the quandle operation, beginning with $s$ and having $m$ factors. **The presentation conjecture.** The Dehn quandle $\mathcal{D}(S^{\mathcal{A}})$ has presentation

$$
\mathcal{D}(S^{\mathcal{A}})=\langle S\mid (s*t)_{m_{st}}=s\text{ if }m_{st}\text{ is even, and }(t*s)_{m_{st}}=s\text{ if }m_{st}\text{ is odd for all }s\neq t\rangle.
$$

The claim proposes a uniform presentation encompassing the spherical Artin-group and right-angled Artin-group examples discussed immediately beforehand. Its resolution would determine whether these parity-dependent relations always suffice to present the Dehn quandle of an Artin group.

record.title: Improper conflict-free and unique-maximum coloring conjecture for planar and outerplanar graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of planar graphs and $\mathcal{O}$ the class of outerplanar graphs. Write $\chi_{\mathrm{iCFo}}$, $\chi_{\mathrm{iCFc}}$, $\chi_{\mathrm{iUMo}}$, and $\chi_{\mathrm{iUMc}}$ for the corresponding improper conflict-free and improper unique-maximum chromatic numbers, with respect to open or closed neighborhoods as indicated by the subscripts.

**Improper coloring conjecture.** For the classes $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{O}$, the following equalities hold:

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{iCFo}}(\mathcal{P})=4,\quad \chi_{\mathrm{iCFc}}(\mathcal{P})=3,\quad \chi_{\mathrm{iUMo}}(\mathcal{P})=5,\quad \chi_{\mathrm{iUMc}}(\mathcal{P})=4,
$$

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{iCFo}}(\mathcal{O})=3,\quad \chi_{\mathrm{iUMo}}(\mathcal{O})=4,\quad \chi_{\mathrm{iUMc}}(\mathcal{O})=3.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the currently known lower bounds are tight for all listed improper coloring parameters; the corresponding gaps between lower and upper bounds are unresolved.

record.title: Uniform stable approximation conjecture for the parametric approximation sets
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}_{P}$ be the finite-dimensional truncation of the parametric Hilbert space $\mathcal{A}$, let $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P,M}$ denote the first $M$ sampling functionals in the approximation set $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P}$, and let $\mathcal{T}_{\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P,M}}$ be their approximation operator. Fix the tolerance $\eta$ appearing in the conjecture.

**Uniform stable approximation conjecture.** The sequence $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P}$ is a stable approximation for $\mathcal{A}_{P}$: there exist $s=s(P)\geq 0$ and $C=C(P)\geq 0$ such that, for every $v_{P}\in\mathcal{A}_{P}$, there are $M\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mu}\in\mathbb{C}^{M}$ satisfying

$$
\|v_{P}-\mathcal{T}_{\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P,M}}\boldsymbol{\mu}\|_{\mathcal{A}}\leq\eta\|v_{P}\|_{\mathcal{A}},\qquad \|\boldsymbol{\mu}\|_{\ell^{2}}\leq C M^{s}\|v_{P}\|_{\mathcal{A}}.
$$

Moreover, the smallest such exponent and constant are uniformly bounded in $P$:

$$
s^{*}:=\sup_{P\in\mathbb{N}}\{s(P)\}<\infty,\qquad C^{*}:=\sup_{P\in\mathbb{N}}\{C(P)\}<\infty.
$$

This is the paper's main conjectural stable approximation result. Numerical experiments indicate excellent approximation and stability for the associated sets, whereas a rigorous analysis proving the asserted bounds is not yet available.

record.title: The geometric-to-strict compatibility conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, let $G_K$ be its absolute Galois group, and let $L$ be a number field or a finite extension of a number field over which a semisimple geometric representation is defined. A weakly compatible system of Galois representations is called **strictly compatible** if, for every finite place $v$ of $K$, there is a Weil–Deligne representation over an algebraic closure of its coefficient field whose specializations agree with the Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representations at every finite place of the coefficient field.

**Geometric-to-strict compatibility conjecture.** Any semisimple geometric representation

$$
G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_n(L)
$$

is part of a strictly compatible system of Galois representations.

This is presented as a consequence of the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture together with standard conjectures on the étale cohomology of algebraic varieties over number fields. The source gives no resolution or restricted case sufficient to determine the status here.

record.title: Polynomial-time approximate-root conjecture for circuit-system Gale duals
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$), let $\gamma_{i,j}\in\mathbb{Q}$ and $b_i\in\mathbb{Z}$ for all $i,j$, and consider the univariate rational function

$$
g(u):=\prod_{i=1}^{n+1}\left(\gamma_{i,1}u+\gamma_{i,0}\right)^{b_i}-1.
$$

For coprime integers $u,v$, define the logarithmic height of $u/v$ by $h(u/v):=\max\{|u|,|v|\}$, with $h(0):=0$. Set $B:=\max_i|b_i|$ and $\log H:=\max_{i,j}h(\gamma_{i,j})$. An approximate root is understood in the sense of Smale.

**Polynomial-time approximate-root conjecture.** Following this notation, one can find approximate roots for all the real roots of $g$ in time polynomial in $\log^n(BH)$.

This conjecture concerns the real-solving complexity of circuit systems, which generalize univariate trinomial equations. It is motivated by reductions of circuit-system solving to real roots of Gale-dual rational functions; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Cyclic-invariant restriction conjecture for the Hochschild pairing quasi-isomorphism
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed oriented $C^$-manifold, let $\Omega(M)$ denote its de Rham algebra, and let $\Omega(M)^\vee[-\dim M]$ be the shifted dual complex. Write $\mathrm{CH}^{-*}_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Omega(M),\Omega(M)^\vee[-\dim M])$ for the (weakly) cyclic-invariant negative Hochschild cochain complex, and let $\Theta$ be the quasi-isomorphism appearing in the Hochschild pairing. **Cyclic-invariant restriction conjecture.** For every such $M$, the quasi-isomorphism restricts to a quasi-isomorphism on cyclic invariants:

$$
\Theta^{-1}(\mathrm{CH}^{-*}_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Omega(M),\Omega(M)^\vee[-\dim M]))\xrightarrow{\simeq}\mathrm{CH}^{-*}_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Omega(M),\Omega(M)^\vee[-\dim M]).
$$

The question arises because the preceding discussion establishes the relevant quasi-isomorphism for simply connected manifolds but does not determine whether the cyclic-invariant subcomplexes are preserved. The author explicitly states that an answer is not known.

record.title: Positivity conjecture for generalized quantum cluster algebras
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}(X,\mathbf{h},\Lambda,\widetilde{B})$ be a generalized quantum cluster algebra with initial extended cluster $\{X_1,\ldots,X_m\}$. A Laurent polynomial in this cluster has the form $f(X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_m^{\pm1})$, and $\mathbb{N}[q^{\pm\frac{1}{2}},h_{i,r}(q^{\frac{1}{2}})]$ denotes the coefficient semiring generated by the indicated parameters. **Positivity conjecture.** Any cluster variable $X$ of $\mathcal{A}(X,\mathbf{h},\Lambda,\widetilde{B})$ can be expressed as a Laurent polynomial $f(X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_m^{\pm1})$ in the initial extended cluster $\{X_1^{\pm1},\ldots,X_m^{\pm1}\}$ with coefficients belonging to $\mathbb{N}[q^{\pm\frac{1}{2}},h_{i,r}(q^{\frac{1}{2}})]$. The explicit type $G_2$ expansions preceding the conjecture exhibit this positivity in examples; the conjecture asserts it for every cluster variable of every generalized quantum cluster algebra, while the general claim is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Fox, He and Wigderson's Ramsey goodness conjecture for complete multipartite graphs and books
record.statement:
Let $k,p,t\geq 2$ be integers. For a complete $p$-partite graph $H=K_p(a_1,\dots,a_p)$ with $1\leq a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_{p-1}\leq t$ and $a_p\leq\delta n$, let $B_{k,n}$ be the book graph on $n$ vertices consisting of $n-k$ copies of $K_{k+1}$ sharing a common $K_k$. Define $d_k(n,K_{a_1,a_2})$ as the maximum $d$ for which there is an $(n+d-1)$-vertex $K_{a_1,a_2}$-free graph in which at most $k-1$ vertices have degree less than $d$. **Fox, He and Wigderson's conjecture.** For every $k,p,t\geq 2$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that for all $n\geq 1$, whenever $1\leq a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_{p-1}\leq t$ and $a_p\leq\delta n$, 
$$
r(K_p(a_1,\dots,a_p),B_{k,n})=(p-1)(n-1)+d_k(n,K_{a_1,a_2})+1.
$$
 This extends known Ramsey-goodness results for books without using the regularity lemma; the conjecture is stated as open in the source, although the paper notes that it fails in many cases and remains open for $a_1\geq2$.

record.title: Kalfagianni–Tran's Strong Slope Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$ with maximum colored-Jones degree

$$
\delta_K(n)=a(n)n^2+b(n)n+c(n).
$$

Set

$$
js(K)=\{4a(n)\mid n\in\mathbb{N}\}.
$$

For a Jones slope $p/q\in js(K)$ with $q>0$, say that it satisfies $SS(n)$ if there is an essential surface $F_n$ in the exterior of $K$ such that $F_n$ has boundary slope $4a(n)=p/q$ and

$$
2b(n)=\frac{\chi(F_n)}{|\partial F_n|q}.
$$

Such an essential surface is called a Jones surface.

**Kalfagianni–Tran's Strong Slope Conjecture.** For any knot in $S^3$, every Jones slope satisfies $SS(n)$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

This conjecture strengthens the Slope Conjecture by predicting the Euler characteristic of an essential surface from the linear term of the colored-Jones degree. It is established for various knot families but remains open for arbitrary knots.

record.title: Harris's topological and analytic finiteness conjectures for special components
record.statement: Fix an integer $d\geq 5$. Let $\operatorname{NL}_d$ be the Noether–Lefschetz locus, and let a component be **special** when its codimension is strictly less than the maximal value $\binom{d-1}{3}$. Components may be considered either only as topological irreducible components, ignoring their natural analytic scheme structures as Hodge loci, or as irreducible components with those analytic scheme structures. **Harris's conjectures.** (1) Ignoring the natural analytic scheme structure, $\operatorname{NL}_d$ has only finitely many topological special components. (2) With the Hodge-locus analytic scheme structure, $\operatorname{NL}_d$ has only finitely many special irreducible components. These conjectures concern the finiteness of special Noether–Lefschetz components. The supplied status evidence says that questions about the largest $d'$ for which the conjectures hold for all $d\leq d'$ remain open, so the conjectures are recorded as open.

record.title: Bollobás–Leader–Malvenuto conjecture on Turán densities of daisies
record.statement:
For integers $r \geq 3$ and $t \geq 2$, an $r$-uniform **$t$-daisy** $\mathcal D^t_r$ is the collection of sets

$$
\{S \cup T: T\subset U,\ |T|=t\}
$$

where $|S|=r-t$, $|U|=2t$, and $S\cap U=\emptyset$. Its **Turán density** is

$$
\pi(\mathcal D^t_r)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal D^t_r)}{\binom nr},
$$

where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal D^t_r)$ is the maximum size of a family of $r$-element subsets of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ containing no copy of $\mathcal D^t_r$.

**Bollobás–Leader–Malvenuto conjecture.** For all $t\geq 2$,

$$
\lim_{r\to\infty}\pi(\mathcal D^t_r)=0.
$$

This conjecture was made by Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto, and independently by Bukh. It remains open even for $t=2$; for comparison, the first unknown case is $\pi(\mathcal D^2_3)$, for which the known lower bound is $1/2$.

record.title: Minimal spectral abscissa conjecture for scalar linear systems with two delays
record.statement:
Consider the scalar linear delay system with two delayed feedback terms, with real coefficients $a_0,a_1,a_2$ and positive delays $\tau_1,\tau_2$. Let $\alpha_{\min}$ denote the infimum of the spectral abscissa over the choices of $a_1$ and $a_2$.

**Two-delay minimal spectral abscissa conjecture.** For arbitrary $a_1,a_2\in\mathbb{R}$, the minimal spectral abscissa is

$$
\alpha_{\min}=a_0-\frac{1}{\tau_1}-\frac{1}{\tau_2}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that two delayed feedback terms attain the natural extension of the one-delay minimum, supporting the use of multiple delays to improve stability without an explosion in the feedback coefficients. The paper notes that an analogous result for more than two delays may fail without bounds on the delays; the two-delay claim is left as a conjecture.

record.title: Fox–Luo–Wigderson's dependence-on-the-ground-graph conjecture for blowup Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $r,t\geq 2$. Write $G\stackrel{r}{\to}H$ when every $r$-colouring of the edges of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. For $t\in\mathbb{N}$, let $H[t]$ be the $t$-blowup of $H$, and let $B(G\stackrel{r}{\to}H;t)$ be the minimum $n$ such that every $r$-colouring of the edges of $G[n]$ contains a monochromatic canonical copy of $H[t]$.

**Fox–Luo–Wigderson's conjecture.** There exists a graph $H$ and integers $r,t\geq 2$ such that there are graphs $G_1,G_2,\dots$ with $G_i\stackrel{r}{\to}H$ for every $i$ and

$$
\sup_i B(G_i\stackrel{r}{\to}H;t)=\infty.
$$

This asserts that the dependence on the ground graph $G$ in the upper bound for blowup Ramsey numbers is necessary for some graphs $H$. The source gives the more specific prediction that this holds for a triangle with $r=t=2$.

record.title: Convergence to steady states in symmetric nonlocal advection-diffusion systems
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a kernel satisfying

$$
\lVert K\lVert_{L^{\infty}} < \infty,
$$

and let the interaction coefficients satisfy $\gamma_{ij}=\gamma_{ji}$ for all $i,j=1,\dots,N$. For any initial datum $u_0=(u_{1,0},\dots,u_{N,0})\in L^1(\mathbb{T})^N$ that is positive in each component, let $\mathbf{u}$ be the corresponding solution of the system.

**Steady-state convergence conjecture.** The solution $\mathbf{u}$ converges towards a steady state.

The conjecture concerns the long-time behaviour of symmetric multi-species nonlocal advection-diffusion systems. Energy monotonicity guarantees convergence of the energy to a finite minimum, but does not establish convergence of every solution to a steady state; numerical investigations have observed stable steady states and no perpetually fluctuating solutions. The problem is left open.

record.title: The Edge-Wilson 25% speed-up conjecture for transitive graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a transitive graph. Wilson's algorithm is said to take asymptotically half as much time to construct the first branch when initialized with an edge rather than a single vertex if the corresponding first-branch construction time is asymptotically half that for a single-vertex initial condition.

**Edge-Wilson speed-up conjecture.** If Wilson's algorithm has this property on $G$, then the expected time taken by Edge-Wilson$(G)$ is asymptotically $25\%$ less than the expected time taken by Wilson$(G,\varnothing)$, Wilson's algorithm on $G$.

The conjecture formalizes the heuristic that Edge-Wilson saves half the time spent constructing the first branch while requiring the same time as Wilson's algorithm to complete the tree. The stated examples motivating it include complete graphs, complete balanced bipartite graphs, and high-dimensional hypercubes; no resolution is given here.

record.title: The non-uniform 1-factorability congruence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $cmathcal{L}$ be a set of distinct positive integers whose largest element is $k$. The non-uniform set system $cbinom{[n]}{cmathcal{L}}$ consists of the subsets of $[n]$ whose sizes belong to $cmathcal{L}$, and it is **1-factorable** when its edges can be partitioned into 1-factors. **The non-uniform 1-factorability congruence conjecture.** Depending on the choice of $cmathcal{L}$, exactly one of the following statements must be true:

$$
\text{(i) For sufficiently large }n,\ \binom{[n]}{\mathcal{L}}\text{ is 1-factorable if and only if }n\equiv 0\pmod{k};
$$

or

$$
\text{(ii) For sufficiently large }n,\ \binom{[n]}{\mathcal{L}}\text{ is 1-factorable if and only if }n\equiv 0,-1\pmod{k}.
$$

The preceding results establish the relevant factorability results in the cases treated, while the conjecture seeks a complete classification for every choice of $cmathcal{L}$; in particular, the behavior when $k-1\in\mathcal{L}$ can differ between the two scenarios.

record.title: The positively correlated random-subgraph independence conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\mu$ be the uniform measure on $V(G)$ and let ${\cal I}(G)$ be the family of independent sets. Define

$$
\bar{\alpha}(G)=\max_{I\in{\cal I}(G)}\mu(I).
$$

Let ${\cal D}_r$ be the distributions on subsets $R\subseteq[r]$ in which each index belongs to $R$ with probability $1/2$ and these membership events are positively correlated. For a cover $V(G)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rV_i$, define

$$
\alpha^*(G)=\max_{r,D\in{\cal D}_r,V(G)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rV_i}E_{R\sim D}\left[\max_{I\in{\cal I}(G)}\mu\left(I\cap\bigcup_{i\in R}V_i\right)\right],
$$

and let

$$
\epsilon^*(\alpha)=\inf_{G:\,\bar{\alpha}(G)\geq\alpha}\{\bar{\alpha}(G)-\alpha^*(G)\}.
$$

**Random-subgraph independence conjecture.** $\epsilon^*(\alpha)>0$ for all $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$.
This conjecture would provide a uniform drop in the largest independent-set density after positively correlated random restrictions and would imply decay of independence densities in Hamming powers of Kneser graphs. The paper does not establish it.

record.title: The partitioned blocker conjecture for almost-maximum independent sets
record.statement:
Let $\alpha>0$. There exist a positive integer $B$, numbers $\tau>0$, $\delta>0$, and $\epsilon>0$ with $\tau4^{-B}>\delta$, such that for all sufficiently large $n$, if $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices whose maximum independent sets have size $\alpha n$, and ${\cal I}$ is the family of maximal independent sets of size at least $(\alpha-\epsilon)n$, then ${\cal I}$ can be partitioned into at most $2^{\delta n}$ parts. For each part $I_j$, there is a family of $\tau n$ pairwise disjoint sets of size $B$, each intersecting every member of $I_j$. **Partitioned blocker conjecture.** The stated partition and blocker family exist for every $\alpha>0$.
This is proposed as a strengthening intended to imply the paper's other independence-set conjecture. The source gives no resolution, so it remains open.

record.title: Quantitative restricted partition conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
For $\varepsilon>0$, a graph $G$ is $(N,\varepsilon)$-restricted if its vertex set can be partitioned into at most $N$ subsets that are $\varepsilon$-restricted in $G$, where a subset is $\varepsilon$-restricted if one of its induced subgraph or complement has maximum degree at most $\varepsilon$ times its size. Let $\operatorname{ind}_H(G)$ denote the number of copies of a graph $H$ in $G$. **Quantitative restricted partition conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ and every graph $H$, there exist $N=N(H,\varepsilon)>0$ and $\kappa=\kappa(H,\varepsilon)>0$ such that every graph $G$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{ind}_H(G)\leq\kappa\abs{G}^{\abs H}
$$

is $(N,\varepsilon)$-restricted. This would unify Nikiforov's quantitative theorem with the qualitative restricted-partition theorem and substantially strengthen the corresponding weakly restricted result.

record.title: Szemerédi–Petruska's sharp bound for $(n,m)$-structures
record.statement:
Let ${\cal N} = \{N_1,\ldots,N_\ell\}$ be a collection of $k$-subsets of a finite set $V$ with $|V|=n$, where $\ell\geq 2$, $k\geq 3$, and $m=n-k$. Suppose that $\bigcap_{i=1}^{\ell}N_i=\varnothing$ while $\bigcap_{j\ne i}N_j\ne\varnothing$ for every $i$, and that every subset $S\subseteq V$ with $|S|\geq k+1$ contains a $3$-element subset not contained in any $N_i$. Such a collection is called an **$(n,m)$-structure**. **Szemerédi–Petruska's conjecture.** Every $(n,m)$-structure satisfies

$$
n\leq {m+2\choose 2}.
$$

This sharpens the previously known quadratic bounds for the order of the associated $3$-uniform hypergraphs and is equivalent to determining the maximum order of a $\tau$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph with transversal number $m$. The paper proves the bound asymptotically, obtaining $n\leq {m+2\choose 2}+O(m^{5/3})$, but the exact inequality remains open.

record.title: Lewis's Hurwitz-orbit classification conjecture for finite Coxeter groups
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group and let $g\in W$ be an arbitrary element. A **reflection factorization** of $g$ is a tuple of reflections whose product is $g$, and the **Hurwitz action** acts on such factorizations by the standard Hurwitz moves. For a factorization $(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$, let

$$
H=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_k\rangle\leq W
$$

and consider the multiset of $H$-conjugacy classes of its factors.

**Lewis's conjecture.** Two reflection factorizations of $g$ belong to the same Hurwitz orbit if and only if they generate the same subgroup $H\leq W$ and have the same multiset of $H$-conjugacy classes.

The product, generated subgroup, and multiset of conjugacy classes are evident invariants of the Hurwitz action. The conjecture was originally posed for complex reflection groups, but the source notes counterexamples for minimum-length reflection factorizations in two exceptional complex reflection groups; the finite Coxeter-group formulation is the claim considered here.

record.title: Liu–You–Tang–Liu conjecture on the exponential reduced Sombor index
record.statement:
Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a graph, let $d(v)$ denote the degree of $v$, and let $T$ be a chemical tree, meaning that $d_T(v)\leq 4$ for every vertex $v$. Write ${\cal CT}_n$ for the set of chemical trees of order $n$, and define the exponential reduced Sombor index by

$$
e^{SO_{red}}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}e^{\sqrt{(d(u)-1)^2+(d(v)-1)^2}}.
$$

**Liu–You–Tang–Liu's conjecture.** For every $T\in {\cal CT}_n$ with $n\geq 5$,

$$
e^{SO_{red}}(T)\leq \left\{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{2}{3}(n+1)e^3+\frac{1}{3}(n-5)e^{3\sqrt{2}}, & n\equiv 2 (\!\!\!\!\mod 3);\\ \frac{1}{3}(2n+1)e^3+\frac{1}{3}(n-13)e^{3\sqrt{2}}+3 e^{\sqrt{13}}, & n\equiv 1 (\!\!\!\!\mod 3);\\ \frac{1}{3}ne^3+\frac{1}{3}(n-9)e^{3\sqrt{2}}+2 e^{\sqrt{10}}, & n\equiv 0 (\!\!\!\!\mod 3). \end{array}\right.
$$

The conjecture concerns the maximum exponential reduced Sombor index among chemical trees of a fixed order. The paper's abstract says that its proposed bound is negative, while the supplied status evidence distinguishes it from another conjecture that was solved and says this one remains open; the exact relationship between that evidence and the negative result should be checked.

record.title: Robust Bollobás–Eldridge–Catlin universality conjecture
record.statement:
For $2\leq k$, let $p^*_{k+1}$ denote the threshold function for the appearance of a $K_{k+1}$-factor in a random graph, and let $G_p$ be the random subgraph obtained by retaining each edge of $G$ independently with probability $p$. Let $k$-universality mean containing every graph on at most $n$ vertices with maximum degree at most $k$.

This is presented as a common strengthening of the Bollobás–Eldridge–Catlin conjecture and the random-graph universality threshold. record.title: Robust Hamilton-power conjecture at the minimum-degree threshold
record.statement:
For an integer $k$, let the **$k$-th power of a Hamilton cycle** be the graph on the same cyclically ordered vertex set in which two vertices are adjacent whenever their cyclic distance is at most $k$. For an $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $G_p$ be its random sparsification obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$.

The statement aims to remove the positive minimum-degree slack and reach the $n^{-1/k}$ probability scale suggested by random graphs. The supplied material gives no resolution evidence, so its status remains open.

record.title: Discriminator conjecture for half-integer quadratic sequences with coefficient ratio divisible by 3
record.statement:
Let $b$ and $c$ be non-zero integers such that $3\nmid bc$. For a sequence

$$
(\operatorname{qr}(n))_{n\geq 0}=\left(\frac{3c}{2}n^2+\frac{bc}{2}n\right)_{n\geq 0},
$$

let $D_{\operatorname{qr}}(n)$ denote its discriminator, the least modulus for which the first $n$ sequence values are pairwise distinct. **The discriminator conjecture.** For every such sequence, there exists at least one value of $n\geq 1$ such that

$$
D_{\operatorname{qr}}(n)\ne 3^{\lceil\log_3 n\rceil}.
$$

The preceding result rules out the claimed discriminator formula in most cases of half-integer quadratic coefficients; this conjecture concerns the remaining case in which the quadratic coefficient is $3c/2$, with $3\nmid c$ and $c\mid\beta'$ as represented by the linear coefficient $bc/2$. The authors report that they were unable to find any examples satisfying the formula, but the conjecture remains open.

record.title: The spectral-gap obstruction conjecture for non-uniformly hyperbolic local diffeomorphisms
record.statement:
Let $f:M\rightarrow M$ be a $C^{2}$ local diffeomorphism on a Riemannian manifold $M$. For a potential $\phi$, define the transfer operator by

$$
\mathcal{L}_{f,\phi}(g)(x):=\sum_{f(y)=x}e^{\phi(y)}g(y).
$$

A suitable Banach space may consist of Hölder continuous or smooth functions. **Spectral-gap obstruction conjecture.** If $f$ is not a uniformly expanding or uniformly hyperbolic endomorphism, then there exists a suitable potential $\phi$ such that $\mathcal{L}_{f,\phi}$ has no spectral gap property when acting on a suitable Banach space of Hölder continuous or smooth functions.

Uniformly expanding and hyperbolic dynamics with Hölder potentials have a spectral gap and therefore do not exhibit thermodynamic phase transitions. The conjecture proposes that failure of uniform expansion or hyperbolicity can be detected by a suitable potential whose transfer operator lacks a spectral gap, a mechanism connected with the phase transitions studied in the surrounding discussion. Its resolution is not established by the supplied context.

record.title: Refined list Hadwiger's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a multiset of positive integers, let $k_\lambda$ be the sum of its elements, and let $|\lambda|$ be its number of elements. For a graph $G$, define $h(\lambda)$ to be the maximum integer $t$ such that every $K_t$-minor-free graph is $\lambda$-choosable. **Refined list Hadwiger's conjecture.** There are functions $\phi,\psi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\psi(n)=\infty
$$

and, for any multiset $\lambda$ of positive integers, if $k_\lambda\geqslant\phi(k_\lambda-|\lambda|)$, then

$$
k_\lambda-h(\lambda)\geqslant\psi(k_\lambda-|\lambda|).
$$

The quantity $k_\lambda-|\lambda|$ measures the distance between $\lambda$-choosability and ordinary $k_\lambda$-colourability. The conjecture asserts that, once $k_\lambda$ is sufficiently large relative to this distance, the gap between $k_\lambda$ and $h(\lambda)$ must grow without bound. The paper proves this for several families of multisets, but whether it holds for all $\lambda$ remains open.

record.title: The kernel-growth conjecture for optimal OGF coefficients
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}(n,k)$ be a fixed lower-triangular invertible kernel, and define

$$
M_{\mathcal{D},k}(x):=\sum_{n\leq x}\mathcal{D}^{-1}(n,k),\qquad 1\leq k\leq x.
$$

Suppose that

$$
\delta^{1/2}=\inf\left\{\rho>0:\max_{1\leq k\leq x}M_{\mathcal{D},k}(x)=O\left(x^{\rho+\varepsilon}\right),\ \forall\varepsilon>0\right\}.
$$

**Kernel-growth conjecture.** An optimal ordinary generating function $\mathcal{C}(q)$ with integer-valued coefficients, $\mathcal{C}(0)\neq 0$, that attains the theoretical maximum of $\operatorname{Corr}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$ satisfies

$$
\rho_{\mathcal{C}}(n)\asymp n^{\delta}\qquad(n\to\infty).
$$

Thus $\rho_{\mathcal{C}}(n)$ is bounded above and below in absolute value by constant multiples of $n^{\delta}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The conjecture connects growth of optimal generating-function coefficients with summatory growth of the inverse kernel; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Sun's general conjecture on linear and circular restricted sumsets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an additive group with $|G|>1$. For finite subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ of $G$, define

$$
L(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=\{a_1+\cdots+a_n:a_i\in A_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n,\text{ and }a_i\ne a_{i+1}\text{ for }0<i<n\}
$$

and

$$
C(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=\{a_1+\cdots+a_n:a_i\in A_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n,\ a_i\ne a_{i+1}\text{ for }0<i<n,\text{ and }a_n\ne a_1\}.
$$

Let $n>1$ and assume that $|A_i|>1$ for every $i=1,\ldots,n$. The **Sun restricted-sumset conjecture.**

$$
|L(A_1,\ldots,A_n)|\geqslant\min\left\{p(G),\,|A_1|+\cdots+|A_n|-2n+1+\{n\}_2\right\}
$$

and

$$
|C(A_1,\ldots,A_n)|\geqslant\min\left\{p(G),\,|A_1|+\cdots+|A_n|-2n+(-1)^n(1+\{n\}_2)\right\},
$$

where $p(G)$ is the minimum of the orders of the nonzero elements of $G$, interpreted as $+\infty$ if every nonzero element has infinite order, and $\{n\}_2$ denotes the least nonnegative residue of $n$ modulo $2$. This conjecture proposes general lower bounds for the two restricted sumsets introduced by Sun; the source does not state a resolution, so its status remains open.

record.title: Equality of hypergraph and graph zero-free loci
record.statement:
For a positive integer $\Delta$, let $\mathcal U_\Delta$ be the maximal simply connected open subset of $\mathbb C$ containing $0$ that is zero-free for the independence polynomials of all graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$. Let $\mathcal U_{\Delta,k}$ be the analogous set for $k$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $\mathcal U_{\Delta,\geq k}$ be the analogous set for hypergraphs whose edge sizes are at least $k$. Thus $\mathcal U_\Delta=\mathcal U_{\Delta,2}$.

**Zero-free locus conjecture.** The zero-free locus of hypergraphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ is identical to the zero-free locus of graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$:

$$
\mathcal U_{\Delta,\geq 2}=\mathcal U_\Delta.
$$

This asks whether allowing arbitrary edge sizes gives no smaller zero-free locus than graphs. The paper notes that its general zero-free disk theorem gives a disk of radius $\lambda_s(\Delta+1)$ inside $\mathcal U_{\Delta,\geq 2}$, but the equality of the full loci remains open.

record.title: Glock, Kühn and Osthus's Euler-tour threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer with $k\geq 3$. An **Euler tour** in a $k$-graph is a cyclic sequence of vertices in which every $k$ cyclically consecutive vertices form an edge and every edge appears uniquely. The **Euler-tour threshold** $\delta^{(k)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}$ is the least $d>0$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, all sufficiently large $k$-graphs with minimum codegree at least $(d+\varepsilon)n$ and every vertex degree divisible by $k$ admit an Euler tour. **Glock, Kühn and Osthus's conjecture.**

$$
\delta^{(k)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}\leq\frac{k-1}{k}.
$$

The source records that an earlier conjecture asserting $\delta^{(k)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}=1/2$ for all $k\geq3$ was disproved, since $\delta^{(3)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}=2/3$. Thus the earlier $1/2$ conjecture is refuted, while the displayed upper-bound conjecture is presented as the subsequent conjecture.

record.title: Uniform-edge conjecture for the expected maximum matching in random bipartite graphs
record.statement: Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices on each side. A **fractional bipartite matching** is a collection of edge probabilities $x=(x_{uv})$ satisfying the vertex constraints $\sum_v x_{uv}=1$ and $\sum_u x_{uv}=1$. Let $R(x)$ be the random bipartite graph in which each edge $(u,v)$ appears independently with probability $x_{uv}$. Equivalently, let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a doubly stochastic $n\times n$ matrix, with $x_{uv}=a_{ij}$ for corresponding vertices. **Uniform-edge conjecture.** The expected size of the maximum matching in $R(x)$ is minimized when $x_{uv}=1/n$ for every edge. Equivalently, for a random bipartite graph whose edge $(i,j)$ appears independently with probability $a_{ij}$, the expected maximum matching size is minimized when $a_{ij}=1/n$ for all $(i,j)$. The uniform instance is known to have expected maximum matching size $(\gamma+o(1))n$, where $\gamma=2(1-\lambda)-\lambda^2$ and $\lambda=e^{-\lambda}$; the conjecture asserts that this instance is worst among all fractional matchings in $K_{n,n}$.

record.title: Strength–super edge-magic deficiency conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a nontrivial tree. A **numbering** of $T$ is a bijection $f:V(T)\to\{1,2,\ldots,|V(T)|\}$, and its strength is

$$
\operatorname{str}_f(T)=\max\{f(u)+f(v):uv\in E(T)\}.
$$

The strength of $T$ is

$$
\operatorname{str}(T)=\min_f\operatorname{str}_f(T),
$$

where the minimum is over all numberings, and $\mu_s(T)$ denotes the super edge-magic deficiency of $T$. **Strength–super edge-magic deficiency conjecture.** For every nontrivial tree $T$, there exists some positive constant $c$ such that

$$
\operatorname{str}(T)\geq c\cdot\mu_s(T)+|V(T)|+1.
$$

The paper notes that the known equality $\operatorname{str}(T)=|V(T)|+1$ for every nontrivial tree would make this conjecture imply the conjecture that every nontrivial tree is super edge-magic. Its status is not resolved in the source.

record.title: The weighted clique-packing conjecture for uniform weights on a clique independent set
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $m\geq 1$ and $k\geq 2$, and let $w$ be an $m$-weighting of $G$. A **$k$-clique independent set** is a set $I$ of vertices such that every $k$-clique of $G$ contains exactly one vertex of $I$. An $m$-weighting $w'$ is **uniform on $I$** when the weights assigned by $w'$ to the vertices of $I$ are equal. **Weighted clique-packing conjecture.** There exist a $k$-clique independent set $I$ of $G$ and an $m$-weighting $w'$ of $G$ uniform on $I$ such that

$$
\pi_k(G(w'))\leq\pi_k(G(w)).
$$

for every $m$-weighting $w$ of $G$. The preceding theorems establish the analogous minimization statement for several graph classes, while the theorem for $k=3$ shows that uniformity on all vertices need not attain the minimum; the conjecture proposes that uniformity on a suitable $k$-clique independent set always suffices.

record.title: The maximality conjecture for Gaussian Riemann derivatives
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $D_{\mathcal{A}}$ be an $n$-th generalized Riemann differentiation without excess. A generalized Riemann differentiation is called **Gaussian** when it is one of the Gaussian Riemann derivatives introduced in the paper, and **symmetric Gaussian** when it is the corresponding symmetric derivative. For a function $f$ and point $x$, write $f_{(k)}(x)$ and $f_{(k)}^s(x)$ for the $k$-th Peano and symmetric Peano derivatives, respectively.

**Maximality conjecture for Gaussian Riemann derivatives.** For all functions $f$ and points $x$:

1. If $D_{\mathcal{A}}$ is not Gaussian, then

$$
\text{both }f_{(n-1)}(x)\text{ and }D_{\mathcal{A}}f(x)\text{ exist}\ \Longrightarrow\ f_{(n)}(x)\text{ exists}
$$

should be false.

2. If $n\geq 3$ and $D_{\mathcal{A}}$ is symmetric but not symmetric Gaussian, then

$$
\text{both }f_{(n-2)}^s(x)\text{ and }D_{\mathcal{A}}f(x)\text{ exist}\ \Longrightarrow\ f_{(n)}^s(x)\text{ exists}
$$

should be false.

The conjecture identifies the Gaussian and symmetric Gaussian derivatives as the largest classes for which the generalized Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund equivalences can hold. Part (i) is known for $n=1,2$ and remains open for $n\geq 3$; part (ii) is false for $n=1,2$, true for $n=3,4$, and remains open for $n\geq 5$.

record.title: Bondy's reverse degree-sum conjecture for long cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with minimum degree $\Greekmath 010E $ and connectivity $\Greekmath 0114 $, where $1\leq\Greekmath 0114 \leq\Greekmath 010E $. Let $C$ be a longest cycle in $G$, let $c=|C|$, and let $\overline{p}$ be the order of a longest path in $G-C$. For a positive integer $r$, let $\Greekmath 011B _r$ denote the minimum degree sum of an independent set of $r$ vertices.

**Bondy's reverse degree-sum conjecture.** If $\overline{p}\geq\Greekmath 0114 -1$, then

$$
c\geq\Greekmath 011B _\Greekmath 0114 -\Greekmath 0114 (\Greekmath 0114 -2).
$$

This is the long-cycle analogue of Bondy's path version. The cases $\Greekmath 0114 =1,2,3,4$ have the cited partial results of Dirac, Bondy, Bermond, Linial, Fraisse, Yung, and Chiba, Tsugaki, and Yamashita; the general statement is not reported as resolved here.
